'''Solomon Jamar Hill''' (born March 18, 1991) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played 9 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]].

==High school career==
Hill attended [[Fairfax High School (Los Angeles)|Fairfax High School]] in Los Angeles. As a junior, he averaged 10.7 points and 8.7 rebounds per game. As a senior, he averaged 16.2 points, 11.7 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game. He finished his career as a two-time Los Angeles All-City selection and a third team all-state pick in 2009.<ref name=bio>{{cite web | url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30700&ATCLID=207985393 | title=#44 Solomon Hill | work=ArizonaWildcats.com | access-date=July 6, 2014}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Hill was listed as the No. 3 small forward and the No. 27 player in the nation in 2009.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/79487 | title=Solomon Hill | work=Rivals.com | access-date=April 6, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], he was a steady contributor for the Wildcats both starting and off the bench. In 31 games (21 starts), he averaged 6.7 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 25.3 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name=stats>{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/solomon-hill-1.html | title=Solomon Hill Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com | access-date=July 6, 2014}}</ref>

In his sophomore season, he was one of just three Wildcats to start every game. He was named to iBN Sports Las Vegas Invitational all-tournament team after averaging 11.0 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.8 assists in event's four games. Head coach [[Sean Miller]] called Hill Arizona's most improved player in 2010–11. In 38 games (all starts), he averaged 8.0 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 25.2 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his junior season, he was named to the All-Pac-12 first team, the NABC All-District 20 first team and the Pacific Life Pac-12 All-Tournament team. He was also named Arizona's Most Outstanding Player by the coaching staff. In 35 games (all starts), he averaged 12.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.0 steals in 32.4 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his senior season, he was named to the All-Pac-12 first team and the NABC All-District 20 first team for the second straight year. He was also a USBWA all-District IX first team honoree and the winner of the Sapphire Award, given to Arizona's male athlete of the year. In 35 games (all starts), he averaged 13.4 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.1 steals in 33.0 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" /> In December 2012, he was awarded the MVP of the [[2012 Diamond Head Classic]] after averaging 12.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 2.3 assists in the three games.<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==

===Indiana Pacers (2013–2016)===
On June 27, 2013, Hill was selected with the 23rd overall pick by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[2013 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Solomon Hill To Pacers With No. 23 Pick In 2013 NBA Draft|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/06/28/solomon-hill-pacers-nba-draft_n_3518089.html|access-date=July 6, 2014|work=HuffingtonPost.com|date=June 28, 2013}}</ref> On July 3, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Pacers and joined the team for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Solomon Hill, Donald Sloan Signed|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/solomon-hill-donald-sloan-signed|access-date=July 6, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2013}}</ref> On December 29, 2013, he was assigned to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Solomon Hill Assigned to D-League|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/solomon-hill-assigned-d-league|access-date=July 6, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2013}}</ref> On January 4, 2014, he was recalled by the Pacers.<ref>{{cite news|title=Solomon Hill Recalled from D-League|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/solomon-hill-recalled-d-league|access-date=July 6, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=January 4, 2014}}</ref> On April 16, 2014, in the final regular season game, he played a season-high 28 minutes and pulled down a career-best five rebounds to go with five points on 2-for-6 shooting (1–2 3FG) in a win over the [[Orlando Magic]]. He appeared in 28 games during the 2013–14 regular season, posting averages of 1.7 points and 1.5 rebounds in 8.1 minutes per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Solomon Hill Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/2488958/solomon-hill |access-date=2024-02-21 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

An off-season right ankle injury forced Hill to miss the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Pacers Drop 2014 Summer League Opener|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-drop-summer-league-opener|access-date=April 6, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2014}}</ref> On October 9, 2014, the Pacers exercised their third-year team option on Hill's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pacers Pick Up Option on Solomon Hill's Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-pick-option-solomon-hills-contract|access-date=October 9, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 9, 2014}}</ref> On November 8, 2014, he scored a career-high 28 points in a 97–90 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Wall, Nene lead Wizards over Pacers 97–90|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141108/WASIND/gameinfo.html|access-date=November 8, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 8, 2014}}</ref> A week later, he recorded 21 points and a career-high 12 rebounds in a 99–90 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Pacers shake off injuries, beat Bulls 99–90|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141115/INDCHI/gameinfo.html|access-date=April 6, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=November 15, 2014}}</ref> Hill appeared in all 82 games for the Pacers in 2014–15, as the team missed the playoffs with a 38–44 win–loss record. Serving as the Pacers' starting small forward with [[Paul George]] out injured for most of the season, Hill managed 78 starts and finished with averages of 8.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.2 assists in 29.0 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Solomon Hill 2014–15 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hillso01/gamelog/2015/|access-date=April 6, 2016|work=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

In July 2015, Hill re-joined the Pacers for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. He shot poorly in three summer league games, going 18.2% from the field for a 4.7-point-per-game average. Hill's role and production decreased dramatically in 2015–16 thanks to the return of Paul George to full health. He scored in double figures just three times over the first five months of the season before scoring a then season-high 15 points on April 6, 2016, in a 123–109 win over the Eastern Conference-leading [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite news|title=With James on bench, Pacers roll past Cavaliers 123–109|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160406/CLEIND/gameinfo.html|access-date=April 6, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=April 6, 2016}}</ref> Four days later, he recorded his first double-double of the season with 13 points and 12 rebounds in a 129–103 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Turner, Pacers clinch playoff spot with 129–105 win vs Nets|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160410/BKNIND/gameinfo.html|access-date=April 10, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=April 10, 2016}}</ref> In the Pacers' regular season finale on April 13, Hill scored a season-high 25 points and went a career-best 7-of-11 from three-point range in a 97–92 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Solomon Hill scores 25, Pacers beat Bucks 97–92|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/INDMIL/gameinfo.html|access-date=April 13, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2016}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2016–2019)===
On July 21, 2016, Hill signed a four-year, $48 million contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-free-agents-hill-moore-and-galloway | title=Pelicans Sign Free Agents Hill, Moore and Galloway | work=NBA.com | date=July 21, 2016 | access-date=July 21, 2016}}</ref> On February 15, 2017, he scored a then season-high 23 points in a 95–91 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900246 | title=Hill's 23 points, 18 from Davis lead Pelicans past Grizzlies | work=ESPN.com | date=February 15, 2017 | access-date=February 16, 2017}}</ref> On March 17, Hill scored a career-high 30 points in a 128–112 win over the [[Houston Rockets]]. Hill was averaging just 6.5 points per game coming in, having spent most of the season focused on defense.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900419|title=Hill's career-high 30 lead Pelicans past Rockets 128–112|work=ESPN.com|date=March 17, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}}</ref>

On August 27, 2017, Hill underwent surgery to repair a torn hamstring.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20476861/solomon-hill-new-orleans-pelicans-undergoes-hamstring-surgery|title=Solomon Hill undergoes surgery to repair torn hamstring|work=ESPN.com|date=August 27, 2017|access-date=August 27, 2017}}</ref> He made his season debut on March 18, 2018, against the [[Boston Celtics]]. Hill played eight minutes and finished with one assist in a 108–89 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975793|title=Davis leads Pelicans past Celtics 108–89|work=ESPN.com|date=March 18, 2018|access-date=March 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2019–2020)===
On July 6, 2019, Hill, the draft rights to [[De’Andre Hunter]] and [[Jordan Bone]] and a conditional 2023 second-round pick, were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the draft rights to [[Jaxson Hayes]], [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]] and [[Marcos Louzada Silva]], plus a conditional 2020 first-round pick.<ref name="AtlantaNewOrleansRef2">{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-draft-rights-to-deandre-hunter-solomon-hill-conditional-2023-pick-from-pelicans|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Draft Rights To De'Andre Hunter, Solomon Hill And Conditional 2023 Second-Round Pick From New Orleans|date=July 6, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> The next day, the Hawks traded him alongside [[Miles Plumlee]] to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for [[Chandler Parsons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/-grizzlies-acquire-solomon-hill-and-miles-plumlee-from-hawks-190707|title=Grizzlies acquire Solomon Hill and Miles Plumlee from Hawks|date=July 7, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2020)===
On February 6, 2020, Hill was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in a 3-team trade.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-iguodala-crowder-hill-020620|title=HEAT Acquire Andre Iguodala, Jae Crowder & Solomon Hill|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> The Heat reached the [[2020 NBA Finals]], before losing in 6 games to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

===Atlanta Hawks (2020–2022)===
On November 25, 2020, Hill signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Free Agent Forward Solomon Hill |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-free-agent-forward-solomon-hill |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 28, 2020 |date=November 25, 2020}}</ref>

On August 5, 2021, Hill re-signed with the Hawks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks re-sign Solomon Hill |url=https://www.nba.com/news/atlanta-hawks-re-sign-solomon-hill |access-date=February 15, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 5, he suffered a torn hamstring tendon in a 130–127 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. On December 8, it was confirmed to be a season-ending injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hawks' Solomon Hill to miss rest of season with hamstring injury|url=https://www.nba.com/news/hawks-solomon-hill-to-miss-rest-of-season-with-hamstring-injury|access-date=January 13, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref>

On January 13, 2022, the Hawks traded Hill, along with [[Cam Reddish]], a 2025 second round draft pick and cash considerations, to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Kevin Knox II]] and a protected future first round pick.<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks Acquire Cam Reddish |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-acquire-cam-reddish |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 14, 2022 |date=January 13, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hawks Acquire Kevin Knox II And First-Round Pick In Exchange For Cam Reddish, Solomon Hill And Second-Round Pick |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-kevin-knox-ii-and-first-round-pick-exchange-cam-reddish-solomon-hill-and-second-round |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 14, 2022 |date=January 13, 2022}}</ref> On January 19, he was waived by the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks Sign Ryan Arcidiacono to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-ryan-arcidiacono-10-day-contract-0 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 20, 2022 |date=January 19, 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On November 26, 2023, Hill married his fiancée Brandi Byrd. Together, they have three children, with Hill having a daughter from a previous relationship with his ex-girlfriend Ashli Scott, who is currently married to NBA player [[Aaron Holiday]].<ref>{{cite web |title= New dads Solomon Hill, Jrue Holiday grateful to spend holiday season in New Orleans |url= https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-dads-solomon-hill-jrue-holiday-grateful-spend-holiday-season-new-orleans
